focus: A1 v2 plugin API ground truth vs v1 @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.34

graphEvents.label: Which plugin shape loads on both v1 and v2
v2 plugin is define({id,setup}) with domain registry transforms, not a Hooks bag
bundled v2 preview types are incomplete versus the 2.0.32 documented surface

label: v2 replaces the v1 flat Hooks bag with Plugin.define({id,setup}) plus per-domain transform registries returning Registration{dispose}; the callable contract differs (function vs object), so a single module cannot trivially satisfy both hosts without an adapter, and v2's acceptance of a callable carrying setup is unverified.

The v2 runtime package is the distinct npm name @opencode/plugin (latest 2.0.32), while @opencode-ai/plugin is at 1.19.3; the repo pins @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.34, one minor behind the stated 1.19.x target, and that v1 package already exports ./v2/promise and ./v2/effect type-preview subpaths.

The v2 type preview bundled in @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.34 declares PluginContext with only options, agent, aisdk, catalog, command, integration, plugin, reference and skill, omitting app, location, session, tool, permission, provider, model, mcp, credential, generate and storage that the 2.0.32 docs document; type-checking a port against the local preview would omit most of the real v2 API.

Plugin registration config diverges on the key: v1 Config.plugin is Array<string | [string, PluginOptions]> (singular) while v2 documents a plural plugins array accepting strings, pkg@version, paths, file URLs and a {package, options} object form, so one opencode.json cannot express registration identically unless each host tolerates the other's key (unverified).

The repo fleet is exactly 16 top-level plain-JavaScript plugin modules under .opencode/plugins/ (a symlink to ../.skilled/plugins) loaded by a non-recursive flat glob, so porting is an in-place edit per file with no build step or generated .d.ts to keep in sync.

Three v1 capabilities have no documented v2 home: the shell.env hook, the chat.message/chat.params/chat.headers mutators, and the experimental.* family; the PluginInput BunShell ($) also appears absent, while setup's returned cleanup function replaces the dispose hook.
Any dual-compat port must be validated against the real @opencode/plugin 2.0.32 types, never against the incomplete v2 preview bundled in @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.34.
Plugin entrypoints remain plain JS with no build step, so v1 and v2 entry shapes must both be valid at runtime in the same file or in two sibling files.

direction: Treating the v2 API as a renamed v1 Hooks object with feature-detected hook keys
reason: The v2 contract is {id, setup} returning a Registration-based domain registry; the callable shape differs, so hook-key feature detection cannot bridge it.

label: The append gateway accepts the full iteration record and returns ok:true, but its state-log projection rewrites it into a reduced schema (type, iteration, run, status, newInfoRatio, ruledOut, timestamp), dropping runId/sessionId/lineageId, focus, mode, target_agent, answeredQuestions and graphEvents; because the contract requires those fields on the canonical record and the reducer rebuilds the convergence graph from graphEvents, any run relying on the state log alone would show nodeCount 0. The full record survives in this delta file, which is why the delta must be treated as authoritative over the projection.
Graph events and answered-question text must be re-readable from the per-iteration delta file, never assumed to survive the gateway's state-log projection.
